Fits a Cox proportional hazards regression model.

Source: R/acro_regression.R
acro_coxph.Rd

Fits a Cox proportional hazards model via ACRO. This function is designed as a drop-in replacement for survival::coxph().

Usage

acro_coxph(
  formula,
  data,
  weights = NULL,
  subset = NULL,
  na.action = NULL,
  robust = TRUE,
  init = NULL,
  cluster = NULL,
  istate = NULL,
  statedata = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

formula

a formula object, with the response on the left of a ~ operator, and the terms on the right. The response must be a survival object as returned by the Surv function.

data

a data.frame in which to interpret the variables named in the formula, or in the subset and the weights argument.

weights

vector of case weights

subset

expression indicating which subset of the rows of data should be used in the fit. All observations are included by default.

na.action

a missing-data filter function.

robust

should a robust variance be computed.

init

vector of initial values of the iteration.

cluster

optional variable which clusters the observations, for the purposes of a robust variance. If present, it implies robust. This variable will normally be found in data.

istate

optional variable giving the current state at the start each interval.

statedata

optional data set used to describe multistate models.

...

Any other parameters.

Value

Fitted CoxPHFitter results object

Details

Please note that multi-state models (using istate or statedata) and time-varying covariate models are currently not supported.
